p: it came to pass in: We should be no less constant in the preaching of the Gospel than the perversity of the wicked is obstinate in persecuting it.
Iconium: Iconium was a city of Lycaonia.
unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles: Who did not obey the doctrine.

Long time therefore abode they speaking: We should not leave our places and give in to threatenings, or to open rage, but only when there is no other remedy, and that not for our own peace and quiet, but only so that the Gospel may be spread further abroad.
fled unto Lystra and Derbe: It is sometimes proper to flee dangers, at the appropriate times.

And there sat a certain man: It is an old subtlety of the devil, either to cause the faithful servants of God to be immediately banished, or to be worshipped as idols: and he does this by taking occasion of miracles which they have done.
gates: Of the house where Paul and Barnabas were.
And saying: That is also called idolatry which gives to creatures, be they ever so holy and excellent, that which is proper to the only One God, that is, invocation, or calling upon.
like passions with you: Men, as you are, and partakers of the very same nature of man as you are.
vanities unto the living God: He calls idols "vanities", after the manner of the Hebrews.
Who in times past: Custom, be it ever so old, does not excuse the idolaters.
suffered all nations to walk in: Allowed them to live as they wished, prescribing and appointing them no type of religion.
And there came thither certain Jews: The devil, when he is brought to his last chance, at length rages openly, but in vain, even at that time when he seems to have the upper hand.
And when they had preached the: We must go forward in our calling through a thousand deaths.
Confirming the souls of the disciples: It is the office of the ministers, not only to teach, but also to confirm those that are taught, and prepare them for the cross.

And when they had ordained them: The apostles committed the churches which they had planted to proper and special pastors, who they appointed not rashly, but with prayers and fastings preceding their choice: neither did they thrust them upon churches through bribery, or lordly superiority, but chose and placed them by the voice of the congregation.
And after they had passed throughout: Paul and Barnabas, having completed their journey, and having returned to Antioch, give an account of their journey to the congregation or church.
Attalia: Attalia was a sea city of Pamphylia, near to Lycia.
